http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/01/two-r.text: Two tankers have reported coming under attack near the Strait of Hormuz, a British maritime agency said on Saturday, as tensions between Washington and Tehran over the region continue to build.According to UKMTO, one vessel said it had been "struck by an unknown projectile" while northeast off the coast of Lima, Oman, causing damage to the engine room.No injuries have been reported so far, per the agency.Around three hours later, UKMTO said it had received a report of a second incident, this time northeast of Khasab in Oman."The Master of a tanker reports seeing a large splash and explosion in close proximity to the vessel," it said in a warning, adding that no damage to the ship had been reported at the time.The agency advised vessels in the region to proceed with caution and to dial in any suspicious activity.Authorities are investigating the incidents.The Strait of HormuzThe Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, is one of the world's most crucial oil and gas transit chokepoints, carrying roughly a quarter of the global seaborne oil trade.Tehran effectively closed the waterway following US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February, and it has since become a key factor in the ongoing US-Iranian conflict - despite the "memorandum of understanding" agreed between the two sides in June.On Friday, the US military rejected claims that Iran had reclosed the Strait, saying it remained "open for commercial vessel transit.""Iran does not control it. Thousands of ships have sailed through the international waterway over the past four months," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said.The statement came as US President Donald Trump said he was "losing faith" in the prospect of a peace deal and threatened to hit Iran "very hard.""At some point, they're going to say, 'we just can't take it anymore,'" he added.US forces renewed strikes on Iran earlier this week after a brief pause, targeting what CENTCOM said were Iranian Revolutionary Guard command centers, maritime capabilities, missile and drone facilities, and coastal surveillance and defence sites."The strikes aimed to further diminish threats posed by Iran and its proxies to American forces, commercial shipping, and neighboring Gulf countries," CENTCOM said.The US had carried out 13 consecutive days of strikes on Iran earlier in July in an effort to "degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz."In response, Tehran launched strikes on American military bases across the Middle East, targeting facilities in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar.

https://www.dailysabah.com/arts/hungarys.text: Arts Cinema Music Events Portrait Reviews Performing Arts Hungary’s 'Attila Tent' showcases shared Hun, Turkic heritage by Daily Sabah with AA ISTANBUL Aug 17, 2026 - 2:27 pm GMT+3 A general view of the Attila Tent at the Great Hun-Turk Gathering, Bugac, Hungary, Aug. 16, 2026. (AA Photo) by Daily Sabah with AA Aug 17, 2026 2:27 pm One of the world’s largest yurts, built as part of the Great Hun-Turk Gathering in Hungary, offered visitors a journey through the shared history and cultural heritage of Hun and Turkic peoples. Known as the "Attila Tent," the massive structure, measuring approximately 20 meters (66 feet) in diameter and 7 meters in height, became one of the most prominent symbols of the gathering, which brings together communities of Hun and Turkic descent . The tent, one of the most striking structures at the gathering grounds, welcomed tens of thousands of visitors with an immersive display recreating aspects of Hun-era history and culture. Inside, replicas of archaeological artifacts from the time of Attila, including swords, plates, bowls and jewelry, were displayed alongside an extensive archaeology and anthropology exhibition exploring the shared past of Hun and Turkic peoples. Three mounted warrior sculptures depicting fighters from the period offered visitors a visual representation of the Huns’ military life, while sections of the tent’s interior walls were covered with depictions of battles involving the Huns under Attila’s leadership. From swords and jewelry to battle scenes, mounted warriors and burial traditions, the Attila Tent presented different aspects of daily life and warfare during the Hun period. Visitors view depictions of Hun warriors inside the Attila Tent during the Great Hun-Turk Gathering, Bugac, Hungary, Aug. 16, 2026. (AA Photo) Ritual of remembrance At the center of the exhibition, visitors were greeted by one of its most striking pieces: a massive cauldron representing a funeral tradition associated with the deaths of prominent figures. According to information provided by exhibition officials, gold and silver jewelry belonging to the deceased would be melted in the cauldron and later buried near a river in memory of the person. The ritual was intended not only as a farewell but also as a way of preserving the memory of the deceased, allowing the community to gather again later to commemorate the person. Another major attraction inside the tent was an exhibition titled “From Ordos to Orseg: Treasures of the Huns, Turks and Hungarians,” which drew visitors interested in the historical connections among the communities. A participant holds a bird of prey while riding on horseback during the Great Hun-Turk Gathering, Bugac, Hungary, Aug. 15, 2026. (AA Photo) Next to the tent, the Hungarian National Museum presented an exhibition featuring replicas of artifacts dating back to the time of Attila. 'Golden crown' draws crowds Varga Zoltan, a board member of the Hungarian Turan Foundation, one of the organizers of the gathering , said the tent was deliberately named after Attila, one of the most prominent figures in Hungarian history. “The reason this tent is so important to us is that it hosts all kinds of exhibitions coming from Turan, especially scientific exhibitions based on archaeology and anthropology,” Zoltan said. A replica of a golden crown is displayed at the Attila Tent during the Great Hun-Turk Gathering, Bugac, Hungary, Aug. 16, 2026. (AA Photo) As part of the exhibition, visitors could also see specially prepared archaeological facial reconstructions, he added. Zoltan said the exhibition’s biggest attraction was a “golden crown,” whose origins trace back to the Ordos region. The crown was discovered in what is now modern-day China, Zoltan said, describing it as a particularly significant piece for those interested in the Hun period. “It is a unique masterpiece for people who love and are interested in the Hun era,” he added. Hungarian jewelry designer Lenya Goblarka said the neighboring exhibition featured valuable pieces shedding light on Hungarian history. shortlink copied Last Update: Aug 17, 2026 3:48 pm KEYWORDS great hun-turkic convention exhibition hungary The Daily Sabah Newsletter Keep up to date with what’s happening in Turkey, it’s region and the world. http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/10/the-d.text: Russian airports temporarily closed 993 times in August — an average of 32 times a day — as Ukrainian drone operations forced repeated airspace shutdowns across the country.Industry data shows it was the most disruptive month for Russian civil aviation since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in early 2022.Figures from aviation security firm Osprey Flight Solutions state that restrictions were imposed at 32 airports in August, including Moscow and St Petersburg.Over the summer as a whole, 2,182 closures were recorded — already exceeding the full-year total for 2025.The Insider, an investigative Russian outlet, calculated that the August closures reached more than six times the 2025 monthly average.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines and insurers on 1 September that Russian airspace "is becoming completely unsafe" for civil aviation."We in Ukraine do not want innocent lives to be lost. That's why we are warning our partners: the days of safety in Russia's skies are over," Zelenskyy said.Andriy Zagorodnyuk, a former Ukrainian defence minister, said the goal was not to attack civilian aircraft but to create lasting uncertainty."Ukraine is not seeking to shoot down civilian aircraft, but it is making Russia's skies unsafe for flying," he said in last week's comments to Ukrainska Pravda.The trigger for airport closures is the activation of what Russia calls the "Kover" — Russian for "carpet" — protocol, an air defence procedure designed for rare emergencies that grounds or redirects all civil aircraft when a drone threat is detected in the area.Military analyst Mykhailo Samus, of the Centre for Army, Conversion and Disarmament Studies, said airport closures were part of a broader strategy of economic exhaustion, alongside rising insurance premiums, the withdrawal of foreign carriers and reduced domestic mobility."Airport closures are the new reality for Russian aviation," he said.'Impossible to take off or land'Russia's Transport Minister Andrey Nikitin said no significant disruptions to civil aviation would be allowed, yet operational data contradict his statement.In the first three days of September, an average of 86 flights per day were cancelled in Russia, according to FlightRadar24 — a level comparable to August's worst periods.On the most severe nights around Moscow, between 77 and more than 100 flights were delayed or cancelled in a single overnight period.Passengers have documented the disruption in detail on social media and in regional news feeds."We've been sitting on the plane for an hour, Vnukovo has been closed, nobody is explaining anything," one traveller wrote on Telegram."Pulkovo won't let the flight depart, Moscow won't receive it." another posted. A third passenger said, "The online board is all red, it's impossible to take off or land."Some foreign carriers that had continued to fly to Russia after the full-scale invasion have since adjusted routes or suspended operations.Changes have affected Pegasus, Flydubai and Air India, according to industry media.Passenger numbers on the Moscow-St Petersburg route have fallen by 20-23%, while rail demand has risen by roughly 20% in response.The investigative outlet Agentstvo has noted that the aviation disruption overlaps with pressure on other parts of the Russian economy, including declining oil refining capacity, higher logistics costs and interruptions to warehouse operations caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on industrial facilities.

Police have arrested three British nationals in Orihuela Costa as part of an investigation into the shooting of a man in Estepona, Málaga, during the height of the summer tourist season. Two suspects have been remanded in custody after a man survived a shooting near a beachfront car park in July. National Police have arrested three British nationals in Orihuela Costa as part of an investigation into the shooting of a man in Estepona, Málaga, during the height of the summer tourist season. The victim, reported to be a 31-year-old Lithuanian national, survived after being shot multiple times on 28 July. Reports issued shortly after the attack said he had suffered four gunshot wounds. Police are investigating whether the shooting was linked to a dispute involving drugs. The attack happened at around 5.30pm in a public parking area near the Andalucía Beach residential complex and the Sonora Beach establishment. Several callers alerted the Andalucía 112 emergency service after hearing gunfire. National Police, Local Police and paramedics attended the scene. Emergency workers treated the injured man before transferring him to Costa del Sol University Hospital in Marbella. Witnesses told investigators that those responsible had fled in a dark-coloured car, giving police an initial lead as they began tracing the vehicle and identifying its occupants. The beachfront location and timing of the attack caused alarm in an area busy with residents and holidaymakers. The management of the nearby Sonora Beach establishment later said the shots had been fired in the parking area, away from its premises. Staff helped the wounded man until paramedics arrived, it said. Investigators followed leads from the Costa del Sol to Orihuela Costa. Officers working on the case, supported by police in Alicante province, searched several homes in the La Zenia area and arrested three British suspects. According to sources close to the investigation, the searches uncovered suspected false documents, weapons and a small quantity of drugs. Police will examine the seized material to establish whether it is connected to the Estepona attack. That includes determining whether any of the weapons recovered could have been used in the shooting. The three suspects were taken into custody and subsequently appeared before the duty judge in Orihuela. Two were remanded in custody, while the third was released on bail pending further investigation. The allegations being investigated include attempted murder, membership of a criminal organisation, drug trafficking, document forgery, theft, vehicle theft and illegal possession of firearms. Authorities have not publicly specified which allegations relate to each of the three suspects or the precise role police believe each person played. Two of the detainees were represented in court by lawyer Roberto Sánchez Martínez. One of those two was the suspect released on bail. Police have reportedly made further arrests on the Costa del Sol, although details of those cases have not been released. Investigators are continuing to reconstruct the events before and after the shooting, including the suspects’ movements and the route taken by those who fled the scene. A central question is the motive. Investigators are examining a possible drug-related settling of scores, but the circumstances of the attack and the degree of involvement of each suspect have yet to be established. The discovery of drugs, documents and weapons during the La Zenia searches does not, by itself, establish how any of those items relate to the shooting. The investigation remains open and is subject to a secrecy order, limiting the information authorities can disclose while inquiries continue. Police have not ruled out identifying or arresting others who may have been involved. For the Estepona victim, the attack ended in survival despite his injuries. For investigators, the work now is to determine who carried out the shooting, who helped them escape and why the violence occurred in a public place beside the beach.
